# Turbine ORM

> Turbine is a Postgres-first TypeScript ORM with a Prisma-like API (findMany, findUnique, with, where), designed for a database that has real data in it: a read-only-by-default Studio, PII tagged in the schema and enforced in the emitted SQL, errors that carry keys and never values, destructive migrations that require consent, and offline missing-index advice. It carries exactly one runtime dependency (pg). Optional SQLite, MySQL, SQL Server, and PowDB engines expose the same typed API behind subpath exports.

Turbine is designed to be legible to AI coding agents: a deterministic codegen flow (introspect the database, generate a typed client, query through it), fully typed query arguments that make invalid queries a compile error, and a stable typed error system (codes TURBINE_E001 through E018) that agents can branch on instead of parsing messages. Point an agent at this file and the docs below to teach it how to use Turbine correctly.

Key facts:
- Postgres-first. PostgreSQL 14+ is the supported floor, which is what CI tests (14, 15, 16, 17). Node.js 20+ (the SQLite engine needs Node 22.5+).
- Exactly one runtime dependency: pg. Optional engines load their drivers lazily and never ship to Postgres users.
- Nested relations resolve in a single statement, via json_agg plus correlated subqueries. This is table stakes rather than a differentiator: Drizzle compiles relational queries to LEFT JOIN LATERAL plus JSON aggregation, Prisma does the same under its relationJoins preview flag, and Kysely ships jsonArrayFrom helpers. Do not describe it as something other ORMs cannot do.
- Studio (`npx turbine studio`) is read-only by default: loopback bound, 192-bit per-process token, every read inside BEGIN READ ONLY, no raw-SQL surface, and the write endpoints are not registered at all unless `--write` is passed. PII-tagged columns are redacted server-side.
- PII is a schema contract. A column tagged `pii: true` is excluded from every default projection at the SQL level on every engine, and is refused as a groupBy key and as a _min/_max target. `includePii: UNSAFE` unlocks it per read (see the privilege-option rule below; a literal `includePii: true` throws).
- Three query options are PRIVILEGE OPTIONS, unlocked by an imported symbol and by nothing else: `skipGlobalFilters`, `includePii`, `allowFullTableScan`. `import { UNSAFE } from 'turbine-orm'` and pass `UNSAFE`; the array form is `skipGlobalFilters: [UNSAFE, 'posts']`. Every other value that asks for the privilege, `true` included, throws ValidationError (TURBINE_E003), because these options sit next to `where` on the same args object and `db.users.findMany({ ...req.body })` used to let a request body drop the tenant filter, the PII projection, or the empty-where guard. JSON.parse cannot produce a symbol, so parsed input cannot reach them.
- Errors carry WHERE keys, never values, so they are safe to log unscrubbed. The full where object is available as err.where.
- Destructive migrations (DROP TABLE, DROP COLUMN, TRUNCATE, unqualified DELETE/UPDATE, ALTER COLUMN TYPE) are refused by migrate up/down and push until confirmed interactively or with --allow-destructive.
- Fully typed: `npx turbine generate` introspects the schema and emits entity types, Create/Update input types, and a typed client. `with` results are inferred end to end at arbitrary depth.
- All user values are parameterized ($1, $2, ...) and never string-interpolated. LIKE wildcards are escaped automatically.
- Typed errors: every error extends TurbineError and carries a `code`. Retryable errors (deadlock, serialization failure) expose `isRetryable = true` as a const.
- SQL-first migrations tracked in a _turbine_migrations table with SHA-256 checksums and an advisory lock; `turbine push` for fast local schema sync.
- Extras: transactions with SAVEPOINT nesting and isolation levels, real extended-query pipelining (N independent queries in one round-trip), server-side cursor streaming, typed raw SQL, pgvector KNN, LISTEN/NOTIFY realtime, and a read-only MCP server.

Common mistakes to avoid when generating Turbine code:
- `turbine` is NOT exported from the `turbine-orm` package. It is emitted into the generated client; import it from your output directory (e.g. `./generated/turbine`). From the package itself, use `TurbineClient`.
- There is no `tx.pipeline`, `tx.sql`, `tx.$use`, or `tx.$listen`. A TransactionClient has only table accessors, `table()`, `$transaction()`, `raw()` and `schema`. Use `db.$transaction([...])` for an atomic batch.
- `schema` in turbine.config.ts is the Postgres NAMESPACE (default `public`), not a file path. The schema-builder file goes in `schemaFile`.
- Never emit `allowFullTableScan: true`, `includePii: true`, `skipGlobalFilters: true`, or `skipGlobalFilters: ['posts']`. All four throw at runtime and are type errors: the option types are the symbol's type, `Unsafe`. Import `UNSAFE` and pass it, or leave the option off entirely.

## Docs

- [Quick Start](https://turbineorm.dev/quickstart): Install, set DATABASE_URL, generate the typed client, run your first query and nested `with`.
- [Why Turbine](https://turbineorm.dev/why-turbine): The checkable comparison against Prisma, Drizzle and Kysely: what is genuinely different (operational safety), what is table stakes in 2026, and what Turbine is not.
- [Turbine for AI agents](https://turbineorm.dev/ai-agents): How to point a coding agent at Turbine, the deterministic codegen flow, and a drop-in agent-instructions snippet.
- [API Reference](https://turbineorm.dev/queries): Every query method, WHERE operator, nested `with` option, the build* deferred builders, client configuration, and the escape hatches.
- [Relations](https://turbineorm.dev/relations): hasMany / belongsTo / hasOne / manyToMany and how the json_agg nesting works.
- [Global Filters](https://turbineorm.dev/global-filters): Soft-delete and multi-tenancy predicates AND-merged into every compiled WHERE.
- [Nested Writes](https://turbineorm.dev/nested-writes): Create, connect, connectOrCreate, disconnect, set, delete, update, upsert on relations inside one transaction.
- [Transactions & Pipelines](https://turbineorm.dev/transactions): $transaction, SAVEPOINT nesting, isolation levels, pipeline batching, and the full TransactionClient reference.
- [Optimistic Locking](https://turbineorm.dev/optimistic-locking): Version-checked updates and OptimisticLockError.
- [Schema & Migrations](https://turbineorm.dev/schema): Code-first defineSchema, DDL generation, and auto-diff migrations.
- [Migrations in Practice](https://turbineorm.dev/migrate): SQL-first migration files, checksums, and the destructive-statement guard.
- [Seeding](https://turbineorm.dev/seeding): defineSeed, seed-as-code, and the non-interactive CI path.
- [Views & Generated Columns](https://turbineorm.dev/views): Read-only views and generated columns in the generated client.
- [Zod Schemas](https://turbineorm.dev/zod): Generating Zod validators from the introspected schema.
- [Read Replicas](https://turbineorm.dev/read-replicas): Round-robin read routing and the $primary() escape hatch.
- [Typed Errors](https://turbineorm.dev/errors): Every error code (E001-E018) and the retry patterns.
- [CLI](https://turbineorm.dev/cli): init, generate/pull, push, migrate, seed, doctor, studio, mcp, observe.
- [CLI Config Module](https://turbineorm.dev/cli-module): The importable turbine-orm/cli subpath: TurbineCliConfig, config discovery and loading, resolveConfig precedence, seed-file resolution.
- [Database Engines](https://turbineorm.dev/engines): SQLite, MySQL, SQL Server, and PowDB behind the same typed API, and which features stay Postgres-only.
- [Database Compatibility](https://turbineorm.dev/compatibility): PG-wire-compatible databases (CockroachDB, YugabyteDB, AlloyDB, TimescaleDB, Neon, Supabase) and their adapters.
- [Benchmarks](https://turbineorm.dev/benchmarks): Three-way numbers against Prisma and Drizzle on a local PostgreSQL database. Measured once on 2026-07-25 against 0.50.0 and not re-run since; treat as a dated snapshot.

## Optional

- [Vector Search](https://turbineorm.dev/vector): Typed pgvector KNN ranking and distance filters, no raw SQL, plus the exported Vector* types.
- [Realtime](https://turbineorm.dev/realtime): Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY pub/sub via $listen / $notify.
- [Serverless & Edge](https://turbineorm.dev/serverless): Bind Turbine to Neon, Vercel Postgres, or Cloudflare Hyperdrive pools.
- [Turbine + Neon](https://turbineorm.dev/neon): Neon-specific setup over HTTP and WebSocket drivers.
- [Turbine + BataDB](https://turbineorm.dev/batadb): Setup notes for BataDB.
- [Studio](https://turbineorm.dev/studio): The local database UI (npx turbine studio), its security model, and --demo mode.
- [MCP Server](https://turbineorm.dev/mcp): A read-only Model Context Protocol server (npx turbine mcp) that exposes schema, migrations, doctor, EXPLAIN, and sample rows to agents.
- [Observability](https://turbineorm.dev/observability): Query lifecycle events and built-in metrics aggregation.
- [The PowDB Module](https://turbineorm.dev/powdb): The turbine-orm/powdb subpath in full: transports, capability gating, PowQL helpers, schema DDL, introspection, and error mapping.
- [Writing a Custom Dialect](https://turbineorm.dev/dialects): The exported Dialect contract: capability flags, resultStrategy, required primitives, and the additive override hooks.
- [Framework Integration](https://turbineorm.dev/recipes): Next.js, Express, and other runtime integration recipes.
- [Migrate from Prisma](https://turbineorm.dev/migrate-from-prisma): API differences and a migration path from Prisma.
- [Migrate from Drizzle](https://turbineorm.dev/migrate-from-drizzle): API differences and a migration path from Drizzle.
- [Changelog](https://turbineorm.dev/changelog): Per-release detail.
